versions.source: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual 8th Edition / NCCN / UICC
versions.provenance: 8th edition staging, verified against AJCC 8th edition / NCCN guidelines; licensed verification standard. Requires R1 clinical verification before unchecked use.
versions.introduction: Thymic epithelial tumours carry two parallel stagings: the Masaoka-Koga system (I-IVb, based on capsular integrity and invasion/dissemination) still used clinically, and the 8th-edition TNM (T by level of invasion from encapsulated T1a to great-vessel T4; N1 anterior/perithymic vs N2 deep/cervical; M1a pleural/pericardial nodules vs M1b distant). Thymic carcinoma behaves far more aggressively than thymoma at the same stage. Myasthenia gravis and other paraneoplastic syndromes affect management but not stage.

t.label: Encapsulated tumour, or unencapsulated without mediastinal pleura invasion (Masaoka-Koga I)
Invasion of mediastinal pleura (Masaoka-Koga IIa/IIb pleural pattern)
Direct invasion of pericardium (Masaoka-Koga IIb/III pericardial pattern)
Direct invasion of lung, brachiocephalic vein, superior vena cava, chest wall or phrenic nerve (Masaoka-Koga III)
Direct invasion of aorta or arch vessels, intrapericardial pulmonary artery, myocardium, trachea or oesophagus

n.label: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
Metastasis in deep intrathoracic or cervical lymph nodes

m.label: Pleural or pericardial nodule(s), separate from direct invasion (Masaoka-Koga IVa)
Intraparenchymal pulmonary nodule(s) or distant organ metastasis (Masaoka-Koga IVb)

stageGroups.basis: Masaoka-Koga I-IIa: encapsulated or microscopic transcapsular invasion
Masaoka-Koga IIb: macroscopic fat/pleural or pericardial invasion
Masaoka-Koga III: neighbouring-organ invasion, resectable pattern

versions.regionalNodes: Anterior (perithymic) nodes are N1; deep intrathoracic (paratracheal, subcarinal, hilar) and cervical nodes are N2. Pleural/pericardial drop nodules are M1a (not T), and lung parenchymal nodules are M1b.
versions.histologicGrade: WHO types A, AB, B1, B2, B3 (thymoma, increasing atypia) and C (thymic carcinoma, graded G1-G3 by differentiation); Masaoka-Koga stage and completeness of resection outweigh grade for thymoma prognosis.
versions.histopathologicTypes: Thymoma WHO types A, AB, B1, B2, B3; thymic carcinoma (squamous most common, plus basaloid, mucoepidermoid, lymphoepithelioma-like); thymic neuroendocrine tumours (staged by the same TNM).
